instruction: I'm visually impaired and need audio assistance. Could you enable the screen reader so I can hear what's on the screen?

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.click({SCREEN_WIDTH_HALF}, {SCREEN_HEIGHT_HALF}); time.sleep(0.5);

result.command: SCREEN_READER=$(timeout 10 gsettings get org.gnome.desktop.a11y.applications screen-reader-enabled 2>/dev/null); if [ "$SCREEN_READER" = "true" ]; then echo "Screen reader enabled"; else echo "No screen reader enabled"; fi

metadata.explanation: Task requires enabling the screen reader for visually impaired users. Evaluator checks if screen-reader-enabled is set to true using gsettings. Similar difficulty to original task - both are single accessibility settings. Uses existing check_include_exclude metric.
metadata.scoring_breakdown: Binary score: 1.0 if screen reader is enabled, 0.0 otherwise

llm_judge_reasons: Evaluator correctly verifies the instruction requirement to enable screen reader
Getter (get_vm_command_line) directly queries GNOME gsettings for org.gnome.desktop.a11y.applications.screen-reader-enabled property
Command logic is sound: checks setting value, returns appropriate text based on whether screen reader is enabled
Metric (check_include_exclude) appropriately verifies that output includes 'Screen reader enabled' and excludes 'No screen reader enabled' and 'error'
Expected values are semantically correct and match the command output format
Complete coverage: evaluator checks the single requirement in the instruction
Command includes timeout and error handling (2>/dev/null) for robustness
Both getter and metric functions exist in official function directories
